name: GA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Jack running with large financial advantage
Democratic challenger Maura Keller badly outraised
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Jack's incumbency and roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge over Keller, and markets pricing a Republican win at 94% all point the same direction, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting anything closer. The forecast sits near the fundamentals-implied margin, slightly beyond the partisan lean to reflect the incumbent's position.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing single digits would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 3rd District is a solidly Republican seat, and first-term incumbent Brian Jack is running for reelection with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean favors Republicans by about fifteen points, and Jack has raised over $2 million with more than $1.1 million on hand heading into the fall.

Democrat Maura Keller has raised only about $150,000, leaving her with little visibility in a district that has not been competitive in recent cycles. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 94% chance of holding the seat. Absent an unexpected external shock, this race is expected to remain firmly in Republican hands.
